:::{#exm-cauchy-schwarz}
#### A strict case and an equality case

- For $\vecf{x} = (1, 2)$ and $\vecf{y} = (3, 4)$:

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y} &= 3 + 8 \\
  &= 11,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  while $\norm{\vecf{x}}\,\norm{\vecf{y}} = \sqrt{5} \cd 5 \approx 11.18$.
  The inequality is strict, and the vectors are linearly independent:
  $(3, 4)$ is not a multiple of $(1, 2)$, since $3 \cd 2 \ne 4$.
- For $\vecf{x} = (1, 2)$ and

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \vecf{y} &= (2, 4) \\
  &= 2\,\vecf{x}:
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y} &= 2 + 8 \\
  &= 10
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  and

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \norm{\vecf{x}}\,\norm{\vecf{y}} &= \sqrt{5}\,\sqrt{20} \\
  &= \sqrt{100} \\
  &= 10,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  so equality holds.

:::
